title: GitHub-first CI, Playwright E2E, visual artifacts and preview delivery

scope.subject: Cloud-first validation, browser regression, artifact diagnostics and static preview workflows

research_summary: Use GitHub Actions as the authoritative clean-runner backbone, Playwright Test as the mature browser E2E and diagnostics framework, and GitHub Pages Actions as an optional no-extra-token preview module. Keep Vercel as a future per-PR preview option rather than adding an external integration now.

sources.finding: Playwright officially supports CI browser installation and recommends one worker on CI for stability and reproducibility.
Playwright recommends Trace Viewer for diagnosing CI failures and provides DOM, network and action context without a custom browser-debugging framework.
GitHub Pages custom workflows support configure-pages, upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages with Pages and OIDC permissions for static-site deployment.
Vercel provides automatic branch and pull-request preview deployments, but it is an external hosted integration beyond the repository's existing GitHub-only surface.
npm lifecycle scripts provide reusable deterministic build hooks and remain useful as a local and CI composition layer around the repository's existing commands.

search_ladder.conclusion: Vercel provides a mature full preview-deployment product, but requires an external project/account integration that is not necessary for the primary GitHub-only validation loop.
Playwright Test already supplies browser lifecycle, assertions, interception, screenshots, traces and reports, so a custom Chrome CDP/WebSocket testing framework would duplicate mature capability.
GitHub Actions remains the clean-runner authority, while GitHub Pages Actions can consume the same static build as an optional no-extra-token preview deployment module.
npm lifecycle scripts remain useful for deterministic install/build composition, but they are only a component beneath GitHub Actions and Playwright rather than a complete validation system.

candidates.name: Vercel Preview Deployments
candidates.reason: Excellent per-PR preview ergonomics, but adding an external account/project connection is unnecessary while GitHub-native validation and artifact delivery cover the current development loop.

candidates.name: Playwright Test
candidates.reason: Directly replaces the hand-written Chrome smoke with mature browser lifecycle, waiting, assertions, request interception, traces, screenshots and HTML reports.

candidates.name: GitHub Actions PR-diff validation backbone
candidates.license: GitHub hosted service / project policy code
candidates.reason: Already authoritative for repository policy and clean-runner validation; extending its downstream build/E2E/artifact job avoids adding another CI platform.

candidates.name: GitHub Pages custom Actions deployment
candidates.reason: Provides an optional static deployment path using the same repository and Actions identity without requiring a Vercel or Cloudflare credential.

candidates.name: npm lifecycle and repository scripts
candidates.reason: Retain deterministic repository commands as the composition surface, but they do not provide browsers, traces, hosted runners or deployment on their own.

coverage_matrix.capability: Clean-runner browser regression and failure diagnosis
coverage_matrix.decision: Run Playwright Test inside GitHub Actions so browser behavior, traces, screenshots, console/page errors and request failures are reproducible without the user's Windows machine.

coverage_matrix.capability: No-extra-credential static preview and downloadable build output
coverage_matrix.decision: Always keep dist and browser artifacts in CI; add GitHub Pages as a separate optional deployment module so Pages settings cannot block validation.

coverage_matrix.capability: Policy-preserving branch, PR and manual WIP validation
coverage_matrix.decision: Preserve the v3 Machine Reuse Gate as the upstream job and let build/E2E run only after the PR-diff policy gate succeeds.

decision.rationale: Combine the existing GitHub Actions authority with Playwright's mature browser-test stack and an optional GitHub Pages deployment module. This gives the largest cloud-only development loop without custom CDP code or a new third-party deployment dependency.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: Vercel is broader and offers superior automatic per-PR URLs, but it requires an external account/project integration; GitHub Actions plus artifacts and optional Pages already covers validation and diagnosis without that dependency.

decision.fallback: If GitHub Pages cannot provide adequate preview ergonomics, connect Vercel later while retaining Playwright and GitHub Actions as the independent validation authority.
